answer: quartz continuously attests owned, unshared cores on one physical chip; grove sets the requirement to the cube of the operator’s identity count, which island maintains across every key. A second chip, virtual cores or rented hosts cannot contribute. Ten trading clones therefore need a 1,000-core chip, the tenth adding 271 cores to the 729 required for nine, while a first identity needs one. The attacker must buy that escalating chip; fresh wallets only raise island’s count.
